# Vectis 0.5.0

**Vectis has a new cloud. It runs on Cloudflare and only does work when something changes. An idle Mac now holds one quiet connection instead of polling every 30 seconds. Paired Macs need to pair once more after updating.**

## Highlights

### An event-driven cloud

- Each Mac keeps one WebSocket to the cloud. Keep-alive pings are answered without waking anything, so an idle Mac costs no cloud work.
- The cloud signals the Mac when a remote command, query or job arrives. The Mac then syncs once, plus a safety sync every 15 minutes.
- Runner demand runs only on events: a GitHub webhook, a change in free capacity, or a runner finishing. Retries and failed webhook redeliveries run every two minutes.
- Missed-job scans moved to the Mac: once on connect, then hourly for each automatic repository.

### Same commands everywhere

Desktop, CLI, MCP and remote control use the same commands as before. Remote operations still replay on the Mac under the same idempotency keys.

### More honest account page

The account page talks to the cloud directly and says so when it cannot load your account, with a way to retry, instead of loading forever.

## Updating

Installed apps find this release within four hours, and the update waits for active work to finish. Your environments, prepared images and local history stay as they are. Accounts, machines and repository connections start fresh in the new cloud, so on each Mac:

1. Pair again from the desktop app, or with `vectis cloud pair` and `vectis cloud finish`, and approve it on [vectis.kerd.dev/connect](https://vectis.kerd.dev/connect).
2. Link your GitHub account again on the GitHub tab of the account page.
3. Connect your repositories again. Settings such as automatic runners, cache volumes and access policies are chosen again per repository.

Remote control from another machine needs a fresh `vectis login`.

## Compatibility

0.4.0 and earlier apps cannot connect to the new cloud. Update every Mac and pair it again. Self-hosted deployments move from Convex to the cloud Worker in `apps/cloud`, which needs the Cloudflare Workers Paid plan; [Run your own cloud](https://vectis.kerd.dev/docs/self-hosting/cloud) has the new setup.

## Platform requirements and limitations

Apple Silicon Mac with macOS 15 or later. Ubuntu 24.04 ARM64 and macOS 26 and 27 ARM64 guests are supported; Windows 11 ARM64 is experimental. Guests are ARM64; Linux guests can run x86_64 tools through Rosetta when you opt in. Network egress is enforced only for Windows guests.
